newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans to privatise 34 airports by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans to privatise 34 airports by 1999.

text.p: Russia plans to privatise 34 of its 63 federal government-run airports by 1999, while another 23 airports have been privatised already, a senior aviation official said on Thursday.

"We plan to privatise 34 federal airports by 1999 to help them out of financial crisis," Yuri Baranov, Russian Federal Aviation Service's (FAS) head department, said on the first day of an international airports conference in Moscow.

He said Russian airports needed 31 trillion roubles ($5.4 billion) for technical modernisation. "Part of this money will come from investors and the rest comes from the budget," he said, without saying how much budget money had been allocated.
Russia has a total of 756 airports, including 52 which correspond to international standards.

Baranov said that currently Russian airports earned about 50 percent of their profits from aircraft take-off and landing fees against about 25 percent for U.S. airports, which make most of their money from terminal restaurants and shops.
About two percent of Russian airports' profit comes from cargo and mail handling and 23 percent -- from passenger service fees paid by airlines.
"We must change these proportions...and give airports the chance to find new ways of earning profits," Baranov said.

Karl Ruppel, FAS deputy head, said that the government had approved a national development programme for federal government owned airports to 2005. "The main idea of this document is to give airports more independence," Ruppel said at the conference.
